;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2019–2021 Iraqi protests]]
**At least two people are killed and dozens injured after [[Iraq]]i security forces fire upon protesters at Sinak bridge in central [[Baghdad]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/01/iraq-security-forces-kill-protesters-baghdad-200117192553279.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Business and economy
*[[Iceland]]ic [[fishery|fishing company]] [[Samherji]] announces it will cease operations in [[Namibia]]. The company was embroiled in [[Fishrot Files|a bribery scandal]] there that resulted in the resignation of Namibian Fisheries Minister [[Bernhardt Esau]] and Justice Minister [[Sacky Shanghala]], as well as the arrest of two employees of [[South Africa]]n banking corporation [[Investec]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-namibia-samherji/icelands-samherji-exiting-namibia-following-bribery-scandal-idUSKBN1ZH0DF?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[January 2020 North American storm complex|Winter Storm Jacob]]
**An [[avalanche]] at the [[Squaw Valley Ski Resort]] in northern [[California]], host site of the [[1960 Winter Olympics]], kills one person and seriously injures another. [https://weather.com/storms/winter/news/2020-01-12-mid-january-snow-ice-rain-storm-west-midwest-northeast (The Weather Channel)]
**Widespread snowfall and freezing rain across the Midwest leads to travel disruption. At [[Kansas City International Airport]], a [[Delta Air Lines]] [[Airbus A319]] passenger jet slides off the taxiway in icy conditions, while rare snowfall was recorded on the [[Texas Panhandle]]. [https://abc7ny.com/travel/delta-plane-slides-off-runway-in-missouri/5858193/ (WABC-TV)]

;Law and crime
*[[Politics of Lesotho]]
**Prime Minister [[Tom Thabane]] announces his forthcoming resignation after an arrest warrant is issued for his current wife, first lady [[Maesiah Thabane]], who is wanted in connection for the 2017 murder of Thabane's estranged wife, [[Lipolelo Thabane]]. [https://www.sowetanlive.co.za/news/africa/2020-01-20-lesotho-1st-ladys-rise-to-infamy/ (''The Sowetan'')]
*[[Crime in China]]
**A man is [[capital punishment in China|sentenced to death]] for [[murder]]ing a doctor in [[Beijing]] on [[New Year's Eve]]. The murder was the latest in a string of attacks on medical staff in [[China]] by angry relatives blaming them for the lack of medical resources and services. [https://www.asiaone.com/china/chinese-doctors-murder-overshadows-new-law-improve-public-health-care (AsiaOne)]
*[[Killing of the Haynie family]]
**A 16-year-old boy, identified as Colin Haynie, shoots his parents and three younger siblings in their home in [[Grantsville, Utah]], killing all but his father, who then apprehended him at the scene. The [[familicide]] was the deadliest mass shooting in [[Utah]] in 13 years. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2020/01/22/colin-haynie-utah-teen-charged-killing-mother-siblings/4548072002/ (''USA Today'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Brazilian federal government]] secretary of culture, [[Roberto Alvim]], is dismissed after the broadcast of a video where he announces a new national prize on culture. In the video, Alvim seems to paraphrase a speech by [[Joseph Goebbels]], [[Nazi Germany]]'s [[Reich Ministry of Public Enlightenment and Propaganda|''Reichsminister'' of Propaganda]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jan/17/brazil-culture-minister-goebbels-roberto-alvim-nazi (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[Prime Minister of Ukraine|Prime Minister]] [[Oleksiy Honcharuk]] submits his [[resignation]] after an audio clip of him allegedly criticizing [[President of Ukraine|President]] [[Volodymyr Zelensky]]’s economic policies was leaked earlier this week. Zelensky subsequently announces that Honcharuk is allowed to keep his position. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-ukraine-pm-resignation/ukraine-pm-offers-to-resign-after-tape-suggests-he-criticized-president-idUSKBN1ZG0RF (Reuters)]
*[[Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752 protests]]
**At a [[Jumu'ah|Friday sermon]] by [[Supreme Leader of Iran|Iranian Supreme Leader]] [[Ali Khamenei]], his first in eight years, he defends the [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|Revolutionary Guards]]’ accidental killing of passengers onboard [[Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752]] and praises [[2020 Iranian attack on U.S. forces in Iraq|Operation Martyr Soleimani]] for giving a “slap on the face” to the [[United States]]. His sermon comes as public anger mounts against the government for their handling of Flight 752. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/01/ayatollah-khamenei-defends-revolutionary-guard-friday-sermon-200117105420440.html (Al Jazeera)]
*Protesters squat an oil terminal in the eastern [[Libya]]n town of [[Zuwetina]] at the request of tribal leaders, who claim that the [[Government of National Accord]] is using oil revenue to pay for foreign fighters, a reference to [[Turkey]]'s [[Turkish military intervention in the Second Libyan Civil War|sending of troops]] and arms in support of the GNA. The protesters are swiftly condemned by the state-owned [[National Oil Corporation]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-oil/eastern-libyan-protesters-enter-zueitina-oil-port-announce-its-closure-idUSKBN1ZG2B5?il=0 (Reuters)]
